newsitem.title: USA: Albright weighs Middle East trip - officials.
newsitem.headline: Albright weighs Middle East trip - officials.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is considering a trip to the Middle East in the wake of a suicide bombing that killed 15 people in Jerusalem, U.S. officials said on Thursday.
An Albright trip "is an option under consideration", said a senior State Department official who asked not to be identified.
The official said no decision had been made. "How live (an option) it is and how imminent it would be I don't know," he said.

The disclosure that a trip was under consideration came after Albright, just back from an Asian tour, and other top U.S. officials met at the White House to discuss how to advance the peace process after Wednesday's bombing.
U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross had been due to visit the region from Thursday, but postponed his trip indefinitely after the bombing to allow a mourning period in Israel.
Albright has not visited the Middle East since she took office in January, but has vigorously denied suggestions that she is neglecting the region.
